market.title: Texas Senate Winner — 2026
resolutionNote: Resolves once Ken Paxton or James Talarico is sworn in as Texas' next U.S. Senator - Kalshi and Polymarket both track this as a Republican-vs-Democrat market, but Paxton and Talarico are the two parties' confirmed general-election nominees, so a party win is effectively a win for that nominee.
Covers any runoff scenario, though Texas Senate races don't have a general-election runoff - the November 3, 2026 result stands.
Kalshi can close the market early once the winner is officially declared, rather than waiting for the swearing-in.

text: Ken Paxton, Texas' Attorney General, knocked off four-term incumbent John Cornyn in the GOP primary runoff in May - a 28-point landslide fueled by a late Trump endorsement, even though pro-Cornyn spending outpaced Paxton's roughly 9 to 1.
James Talarico, an Austin state representative, is the Democratic nominee, and he's heavily outraising Paxton - over $72M raised since the start of 2025 versus Paxton's $16.8M.
That money gap hasn't shown up in the prediction markets yet: Kalshi and Polymarket both have this close to a coin flip, with Paxton still a slight favorite.
It has shown up in public polling, though - several independent polls through late July and early August have Talarico ahead by anywhere from 2 to 5 points, unusual for a statewide Texas race.
marketBrief.author: Owain Flanders
